chunks: What ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding a pledge, if it is lost while in the possession of the creditor without his having consumed it, he may return to the pledger for his due and take it. But if he consumed it, then the two of them should settle the excess between themselves.

key_terms.الرَّاهِنِ: the pledger or debtor who gave the collateral
key_terms.الرَّهْنِ: a pledged item given as security for a debt
key_terms.الْمُرْتَهِنِ: the creditor or pledge-holder who possesses the collateral
key_terms.بِحَقِّهِ: for his due or legal claim
key_terms.تَرَادَّا: they mutually return or adjust matters between themselves
key_terms.يَسْتَهْلِكَهُ: to consume, use up, or destroy the pledged property

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if pledged property is lost or consumed by the creditor in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning rahn (pledged property held as security for a debt). If the pledged item is lost without the creditor’s wrongful consumption, he may still claim his right from the pledger; but if he consumed the pledged item, then the excess value is to be adjusted fairly between them.
